about: Each change to frozen bridge code against the merge base, with one reason: moved (a rule moved into Rust, naming its task), refactor (behaviour kept), gone (an entry that left the freeze) or main (a change main made, merged by this change: the full SHA of the main commit, then its title). Entries the merge base already holds are spent and may be pruned.

packages/structured-data-models-client/s.moved: T2.8c: main's 1fc5a686 (multi-call predict) moved into the core: rows_per_call joins the options whose values the core reads (TAKEN, VALUED), its type, bound and the batches it asks the core's (sdm-request options, sdm-core materialize); no rule added here

T1.32a: the cast to the key's type with pandas (pd.Series(indices, dtype=...)) and its INVALID_REQUEST and INTERNAL_ERROR split are the core's rule table; the bridge hands over the values as pyarrow infers them, or as their text where it infers no one type
T1.32a: the host's half of the moved cast: which of its own values are missing when it writes them as text (None, pd.NA, pd.NaT, a float NaN), the core reading a null
T1.32a: the bridge's key_type refusal, for a key type it had no cast for, is the core's (sdm_engine::keys::cast refuses a key type no rule casts to)

T2.8c: main's multi-call materialize (1fc5a686) is the core's: the bridge passes the client's MOST_ENTITIES and MOST_CALLS as the contract's most_entities and most_calls (as it passes MOST_PARTS), and takes back each later call's payload and rows from RequestState.batches; the ceilings, the batching and the per-batch walk are sdm-core materialize's

T1.36 fix 4 (the final review's P2-2): the host's half of the moved cast: a float in a mix written as the core now writes a float entity (sdm_engine::keys's float_text), the reference's text of it, pyarrow's cast of the float to text at its own width (1e16 is 1e+16), so the core reads back the number the host was given; a boolean as before

packages/structured-data-models-client/s.refactor: T2.1b: each table named is sent as contract v26 writes a source, a relation of one part (codec.relation), never split on a dot; T2.2: the provider choice and provider are the source's backend's (_provider), SQLite's beside DuckDB's; no rule added

packages/structured-data-models-client/s.moved: T2.8c: the module gains _result (the result's rows as the client's PredictionResult, split out of predict, unchanged) and _carry_the_answers (the core's answered parts, CoreError.answered, put in details as main's 1fc5a686's client puts them: answered, rows_answered); which calls answered and how they are numbered and merged are sdm-core predict's

T1.36 fix 8: the host's half of the moved entity reading: a row's id as the core's id_as_written column gives it (the JSON text of the reference's item value, read as the transport reads JSON), else the id column's value, a missing one None; no rule of its own, as _as_answered for a prediction

T2.8c: a request asked in several calls (RequestState.batches) is predicted by the core in one run: each later call's payload and rows passed with its own request id, drawn with _request_id as the adapter draws one per call; the endpoint's refusal is told to the core by its status (run.Refused) so the core carries the answers before it, and raised with them (E47's text unchanged); main's _numbered_across_calls and _carry_the_answers_already_paid_for are sdm-core predict's. Fix 1: any other exception the transport raises (the Databricks SDK's ValueError for a failed OAuth refresh) is told to the core as a failed call, so it carries the answers before it, and is raised with them, as main's client catches any Exception.

T2.8c: the host's half of main's _carry_the_answers_already_paid_for and _carry_the_steps_already_paid_for (1fc5a686): the answers the core carried (CoreError.answered) read into details['answered'] as a PredictionResult, with rows_answered for a batched request; the core decides what was answered. Fix 1: on whatever exception the call raised, not only the client's own, as main's client does.
